$comment: Every run of this conformance corpus by an implementation independent of the specification's author, one row per posted run. This file is the record the independence column's prose is derived from: scripts/independent-runs-gate.py computes the not-run set as the revisions from 1 to the current suiteRevision that no row here names, and fails when the prose in README.md or docs/IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md names a different set. A row is what licenses a figure in the prose, so do not add one for a run that was not posted with a record. Each figure is transcribed exactly as posted and names every document that carries it, so a figure cannot be quietly inflated in one of them: never rounded, never restated as a fraction of a different corpus, and never re-characterised as unprompted when their author called the run directed. Where this repository does not carry a value it records null beside a note saying so, rather than leaving the field out, because an absent field and an unrecorded fact read the same in a diff.
independence: from-spec Rust verifier with its own I-JSON parser, RFC 8785 serializer, RFC 6962 Merkle root, run-binding derivation and Ed25519 tier, built with no sight of the reference code
currentRevisionSource: vectors/CHANGES.md, the per-revision changelog that owns revision numbering. It is read rather than restated here: a revision number written in this file could only ever agree with itself.

runs.digestNote: the headline figure is the blind first run and no digest names the build that produced it. The checker's reports/INDEX.json carries an explicit null digest for that record beside a sourceUnrecoverable field saying the blind build was never committed on its own -- 46ca0ee carries both the v0.7 implementation and the published number, so no tree in that repository hashes to it -- rather than borrowing the directed build's digest, which would name a different implementation. The report records this as a breach of rule 6 of its own PROTOCOL-v0.7.md, the rule that run's protocol fixed in advance. The directed build IS digest-bound, at sha256:56f440e628ff39e49d92968943c5bce6024503169dfa394671f848f1e98e67e2, and reproduces from the author's working tree; this schema carries one digest per row and the row's headline is the blind figure, so that value is recorded here in the note rather than in the field.
runs.note: the v0.7 run, and the first run posted against a corpus this repository moved to a new predicate version. That report leads with the blind figure and says the directed one is not evidence about the determinacy of the text, so the blind 179/232 is the headline here: accepts 8/54, rejects 169/176, indeterminate 2/2. The directed pass reached 232/232, accepts 54/54, rejects 176/176, indeterminate 2/2, and is directed twice over in the author's account -- it followed a spec diff already read and, for bad-902, an adversarial review of that implementation. The report partitions the 53 first-run mismatches by the message the blind build emitted, and says that is the only partition its published run records support: 42 report that aeeRunBinding does not equal the run binding derived from the statement, 7 returned valid with no reason, and 4 report a carried pass_indirect against a recomputed pass. An earlier per-fix attribution of 43/5/3/2 was withdrawn rather than restated, because attributing a recovery to a particular fix needs a bisection against the blind build and that build is unrecoverable. Three rules the directed pass implemented recovered no vector and the blind run never reached them -- the registered networkPosture.posture vocabulary, non-empty signatures, and attribution as a substrate-row validity requirement, forced by bad-823, bad-745 and bad-968 -- so their correctness in this run is directed and says nothing about whether the text determines them; ok-047 and ok-048 are attribution vectors and both were blind mismatches. The report claims no reason-parity figure for this run at all: that build emits free prose and no condition codes, two constructions over the same run disagreed at 175/178 and 167/178, and the ambiguity is published as a script rather than resolved by picking one. The corpus commit it pinned resolves in this repository and carries the 232 vectors of suiteRevision 22.

runs.note: the run against the current corpus, and the only one in this ledger posted as a thread comment rather than as a run report in the checker's own provenance index. The suite commit resolves here and its manifest carries 250 vectors partitioned exactly as posted, 55 accept, 193 reject and 2 indeterminate, under corpusDigest b5aa5fdb and vendored spec digest 759d2383, both identical to the values at the head of this repository. The run is directed on its author's own opening words, 'Repinned and implemented first, then measured your open question' -- the checker was brought to this revision before it was measured, so the figure says the revision-25 text is implementable from it, not that an unaided reader arrived at it. The indeterminate 2/2 is stated in the prose but is not bound as a figure here, because '2/2' occurs in both publishing documents for unrelated reasons and a count over it would assert nothing about this run. The commit no ref reached is now held by the annotated tag cited/97ba4ff, so a reproducer can fetch it from a clone.

attemptsComment: Every dispatch by that same independent implementation that was authorised, ran, and returned no figure, one row per dispatch. The runs array above is what licenses a figure in the prose, and it has no shape for a run that reported nothing: every element of it carries a figures array, so an attempt recorded there would have to invent one. Recording nothing instead is the defect this file's own $comment argues against, because an absent field and an unrecorded fact read the same in a diff, and a dispatch that produced no score is exactly the fact a reader of the independence column would otherwise never learn was made. So an attempt carries figures null beside a figuresNote saying why there is none, and it carries no suiteRevision at all: the not-run set is computed over the runs array, and a suiteRevision here would shrink that set and let an attempt license the very figure it has none of. What an attempt binds instead is the corpus commit the dispatch was pinned to, the checker ref it ran, the authorization packet it came from, the dispatch itself, and where its artifacts survive with how long for. outcome is a closed token so that 'it did not produce a score' cannot be written two ways: withheld is a gate refusing publication, completed-no-figure is a run that finished and publishes no score by its own design, and void is a dispatch that did not reach a terminal state at all.

attempts.note: the first hosted dispatch, authorised for one run against this corpus at 59faf842 with the seven named sites and the control, and not rerun. Its author reported it as a mistake of his own as well as a withheld run: the packet was built before a fix that had landed the day before, and one reading of the kept material is that the candidate ran as a non-root user against a source directory it could not read, the defect at https://github.com/corpus-adequacy/corpus-adequacy/issues/178 fixed in https://github.com/corpus-adequacy/corpus-adequacy/issues/179. That is a reading of the code and not the only thing that fits what was kept. Whatever the cause, the run produced no finding about this corpus or its Go rail, which is why it earns no figure anywhere in this repository.

attempts.figuresNote: the run publishes no score and no per-mutant result, which its author said before asking for the dispatch and which is a property of the packet rather than of what happened. All nine planned invocations left a record -- by the runner's code the unmutated baseline, the control and the seven site mutants -- each finished and each container was confirmed removed. Nine records is a statement about the runner's ordering, not a measurement of this corpus: the mutants only run after a clean baseline and the sites only after the control was killed, so it says both held, and it comes from the runner's code rather than from a report anyone can read, because the report itself is not uploaded.

quotedWordingComment: The author's wording, transcribed once and checked verbatim wherever this repository says it carries it. Where a document carries a shorter cut of a longer sentence, both rows name the same utterance, and the gate requires every excerpt of an utterance to be a contiguous substring of the fullest form recorded of it -- that is what stops one document carrying a paraphrase that reads like a quotation of the same sentence. utterance names the sentence, not the run: one run's author can say more than one thing, so grouping on about would require two unrelated quotations from one run to contain each other. A row that is the only excerpt of its utterance is checked by the verbatim rule alone, because with one excerpt on record there is no second reading to disagree with.
